investigator.method: Level 1 PASSIVE_STATIC via curl (plain HTTP GET, descriptive User-Agent, no authentication, no browser): retained the homepage and its own linked /contact path (which server-redirects back to the homepage). Level 2 STRUCTURAL: decoded and inspected the page's own inline bootstrap JSON (a Readymag 'data-content' project-configuration blob) for any discoverable event data or API reference.

probe_history.reason: The homepage (https://lokschuppen-berlin.com/) served <!-- Designed with Readymag --> markup: a client-rendered visual-canvas microsite (generator meta 'Readymag', <meta name="robots" content="noindex,nofollow">, page title 'LOKSHUPPEN NEW WEB'). The raw HTML body is only a mount point (<div id="root">) plus a single <script type="module" src="...viewer.js">; there is no server-rendered text content, no application/ld+json, no wp-json, no ICS link, no Fourvenues script, no Sanity config. The linked /contact path 301-redirects back to the same homepage shell, confirming no distinct server-rendered content pages exist on this domain at all.

Decoded the homepage's own inline data-content JSON blob (Readymag's project bootstrap config, embedded server-side in the initial HTML so no JS execution was needed to read it). It contains only visual-canvas metadata for the Readymag page-builder product itself (project id, CDN asset paths, text/style definitions, font/colour settings) -- a design/branding microsite tool, not an events-calendar platform or CMS. No API endpoint, feed URL, or event-shaped data of any kind is referenced anywhere in the retained bootstrap JSON. Readymag is a visual publishing tool (magazine/portfolio-style canvases); there is no known or discoverable public content API pattern for it that would expose structured event records, so guessing one would not be a genuine, evidenced probe.

Kept PARTIAL rather than PROVEN because the first-party evidence alone does not state the venue's identity in text.

blockers.description: The venue's official domain (following its 2024 rebrand from Suicide Circus/Suicide Club to Lokschuppen Berlin) currently serves only a client-rendered, noindex/nofollow Readymag placeholder page with no server-rendered content and no discoverable public API. Neither the homepage nor its own linked /contact path exposes any event, programme, or even static venue-description text at all.

reasons: The official domain is genuinely a placeholder/in-transition microsite at time of investigation (client-rendered Readymag canvas, noindex/nofollow, no server-rendered text, no distinct content pages -- /contact redirects straight back to the homepage shell).
Level 1 (homepage + /contact) found zero usable structured data: no JSON-LD, no ICS, no WordPress/Tribe signature, no Fourvenues script, no Sanity config.
Level 2 (decoding the page's own inline Readymag bootstrap configuration) found only visual-canvas/design tool metadata -- no event data, no API reference of any kind to escalate toward.

No headless browser tool is available in this environment; even if one were used, there is no first-party evidence here suggesting the client-side rendering conceals actual event content rather than an intentionally minimal rebrand placeholder.
Official identity itself is only PARTIAL (corroborated via third-party discovery, not self-stated on the retained page), so activation-grade identity confidence is not yet reached either.

The correct honest outcome is to defer and revisit once the club's post-rebrand site is genuinely live with real programme content, rather than fabricate event fields from a page that currently has none.
